title: Locally constant maps form a sheaf of sets
statement: Let U be a topological space and R a set. A map from an open subset V of U to R is locally constant if every point of V has an open neighbourhood in V on which the map is constant. For each open V let L_R(V) be the set of such maps, with restriction maps. Then L_R is a sheaf of sets on the site of open subsets of U with open coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]: compatible locally constant maps on an open cover glue uniquely to a locally constant map.

source.place: Sheaves, Example 6.4 and Definition 6.5 (Tag 006W): continuous maps form a sheaf; for a discrete target these are the locally constant maps

proof.text: Apply the unique-gluing characterization of sheaves for types to reduce the goal to existence and uniqueness of a gluing for every compatible family.
Use the compatible-family gluing theorem to obtain a locally constant section satisfying all restriction equations.

For uniqueness, two gluings agree at each point by choosing a cover member containing that point and comparing the corresponding restriction equations; extensionality for LocallyConstant concludes equality.
